sets.name: Altissimo
sets.src: The Woodwind Fingering Guide (wfg.woodwind.org), lower and upper altissimo pages (for all sizes of sax unless marked), and Kevin Danenberg’s tenor altissimo chart (marked tenor).

f.d: Kevin Danenberg (tenor): Sounds a little dodgy, but a handy alternate to palm F or front F in passing; works chromatically up through G♯.
Stable for mp and louder on tenor and baritone models, and for mf and louder on alto models.
For alto models. Stable and in tune, but awkward in fast passages.

f.k: 8va Fx L2 Sb R1 R2 R3

f.d: Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor: A nice alternate to front F; easy move to the alternate G.
Use in combination with G6 or the range D5–Bb5.
In tune, easy response, and useful in fast passages. For all saxophone models
Good for tenor. Use in combination with F6 and G6.
In tune and responsive on alto when mouth is tight and jaw is lowered.
Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor: His usual G.

f.k: 8va L1 L2 L3 R1 R2 R3 C
8va L1 L2 L3 R1 R2 R3 Eb

f.d: Good for tenor. Works well in chromatic passages and in combination with F6 and F#6.
Kevin Danenberg (tenor): Alternate; helps in some passages.

f.k: 8va L1 L3 Sc F# R1 Eb
8va L1 L2 L3 C# R1 R2 R3 C
8va L1 L2 L3 Bb R1 R2 R3 C

f.d: Good for baritone. Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor.
Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor: In passing.

f.k: 8va L2 L3 R1 R2 R3 Eb
8va L2 L3 Bb R1 R2 R3 C
8va L1 L2 L3 B R1 R2 R3 C
8va L1 L2 L3 R1 R2 R3
8va L1 L2 L3 Sc R1 R2 R3

f.d: Good for baritone. Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor: Adding the G♯ key raises the pitch and adds pop (or add right hand 1 2 3 instead).
Kevin Danenberg (tenor): Left hand 3 is optional but adds pop and saves finger motion.
Kevin Danenberg (tenor): Left hand 3 optional, as for C.
Good for alto and tenor. Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor: His usual D; resets the hand for D♯.
Good for alto. Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor: Pops a little better and flows with B♭–C♯ (Lenny Pickett).
Useful for alto, especially in quick transitions with C7, fingered by the same fingering.

f.k: 8va Fx L2 L3 Bb R1 R2 R3 C

f.d: Good for tenor. For tenor. Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor: Same as B♭, overblown a fourth.

f.k: 8va Pd L1 L2 Sb R2 R3
8va L2 L3 R1 R2 R3 C
f.d: An effective harmonic fingering. The 10th harmonic on C4.
Kevin Danenberg (tenor): Same as B, overblown a fourth.

f.k: 8va Pd Pe L2 R1 R2 Eb

f.d: Kevin Danenberg (tenor): Same as C, overblown a fourth.

f.k: 8va Pd Pe L2 Se Sc R1 R2
8va Pd Pe L1 L3 R1 R3

f.d: Kevin Danenberg (tenor): Same as C♯, overblown a fourth.
Useful for alto. Requires fast air stream.
Good for tenor. Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor: For him the highest note that pops out easily (Rascher).
Good for alto and tenor. Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor: A little muted (Lenny Pickett).
Good for alto. Can be reached by the 12th harmonic on C#4 or the 14th harmonic on Bb3.

f.k: 8va L1 L2 L3 R1 R2 R3

f.d: Kevin Danenberg uses this on tenor: Rascher.

f.k: 8va Pd Pe L2 L3 R2 R3
8va L1 L2 L3 Bb R1 R2 R3 C
f.d: Kevin Danenberg (tenor): Low B♭ fingering – arpeggiate up to it at first.

f.k: 8va Pd Pe Pf L2 L3 Se Sc R2 R3
8va L1 L2 L3 B R1 R2 R3 C
f.d: Kevin Danenberg (tenor): Low B fingering – arpeggiate up to it at first.

f.k: 8va Pd Pe L2 L3 R2 R3
8va L1 L2 L3 R1 R2 R3 C
f.d: Kevin Danenberg (tenor): Low C fingering – arpeggiate up to it at first.

f.k: 8va Pd Pe L2 L3 R2 R3
f.d: Lip up from C8 to achieve C#8.

f.k: 8va Pd Pe L2 L3 R2 R3
f.d: Lip up from C8 to achieve D8.

f.k: 8va L1 L2 L3 Bb R1 R2 R3 C
f.d: Kevin Danenberg (tenor): A harmonic of low B♭ that just wants to come out.

sets.name: Quarter tones
sets.src: The Woodwind Fingering Guide (wfg.woodwind.org), quarter-tone chart, first and second octaves – for all sizes of sax. Each note is a quarter tone above the one named (C♯4 +¼ = D quarter-flat). Low C♯ to D, D +¼, G +¼ and the notes above D♯6 +¼ have no listed fingering.

L1 L2 L3 R1 R3 Eb

L1 L2 B R2 R3 C

8va L1 L2 L3 B R1 R2 C
8va L1 L2 L3 R1 R2 C
